key_insight: The paper introduces two Lean 4 benchmark suites that measure how well AI agents can produce machine-checkable proofs for quantum algorithms and quantum information, with verified library access improving results across all tested models.
engineering_relevance: For quantum computing toolchains, this provides a reproducible way to evaluate and strengthen formal-proof agents, especially for correctness-critical workflows in algorithms, simulation, and information theory.
method: Built Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench (36 tasks) and Lean-QIT-Bench (40 tasks) for theorem completion.
Evaluated GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, and MiniMax M3 under task-only and library-augmented deduction (LAD).
Used deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review, with difficulty weights fixed before model runs.
evidence_signal: LAD improved both score and completion rate in all eight model-benchmark comparisons, with top difficulty-weighted scores of 60.4/100 on quantum algorithms and 59.6/100 on quantum information.
watch_item: Benchmark performance may not fully reflect real-world proof robustness because results depend on a fixed Lean environment, curated task set, and access to a verified domain library.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
